title: Massaman Curry
subtitle: Slow-cooked beef with potatoes, coconut milk, and warm spices
excerpt: Massaman is one of the milder Thai curries, closer in character to a Persian or Mughal spiced braise than to fiery green or red curry. Beef chuck and potatoes cook slowly in coconut milk with star anise, cinnamon, and cardamom until the sauce is thick and the meat yields completely. Tamarind and fish sauce balance the sweetness of palm sugar.
sourceNotes: Massaman curry is believed to have arrived in Thailand via Muslim traders from the Persian Gulf and Indian subcontinent, likely in the 17th century. The name is thought to derive from the word Muslim in Thai pronunciation.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze without the potatoes (they go grainy when frozen). Add fresh potatoes when reheating.

content.text: The three-way balance of palm sugar, fish sauce, and tamarind is the key to a good massaman. Taste at the end and adjust each one incrementally until the sauce tastes rounded.

items.prepNote: cut in half if small, quartered if large

content.text: Place the beef in the large saucepan and pour over the coconut milk. Add the star anise, bay leaves, cinnamon, and cardamom. Bring to a gentle simmer, cover, and cook for 45 minutes.
Add the quartered onion and potato to the pan. Stir in the palm sugar, fish sauce, and tamarind paste.
Continue simmering, covered, for a further 30 minutes until the beef is tender and the potato is cooked through.
Remove the lid and simmer for 10 minutes to reduce and concentrate the sauce slightly.
Taste and adjust the balance: more fish sauce for salt, more tamarind for sourness, more palm sugar for sweetness. Scatter the toasted peanuts over the top before serving with steamed rice.

items.symptom: The beef is still tough after 75 minutes
items.cause: Beef chuck needs sustained low heat to break down the connective tissue
items.fix: Continue cooking on a low simmer, adding a splash of water if needed. It will become tender given enough time.

items.cause: The seasoning balance is off between salt, sweet, and sour
items.fix: Add a little more fish sauce for saltiness, a squeeze of tamarind for sharpness, or a pinch of palm sugar to round it out.
